messages.subject: Estimate of some parameters flow away (using STAN)
parts:
Hi,
I wanted to fit a non-linear mixed effect model and take into account the left censoring values, so I use Tobit regression for non-linear mixed model.
I used the data on log10 scale for antibody level. The initial antibody level at time point 0 is random, assumed a log normal distribution so: A0,i = A0*exp(bi) where bi ~ N(0, sigmaA0)
Data on log10 scale is assumed to have a normal distribution so: log10(A,obs) = log10(A,pred) + epsilon.
The predicted antibody level could be written down as:
  - If t <=2 then A = (A0*exp(bi))*exp(-beta*t[i])
  - If   2 <t <= h: then A = (A0*exp(bi))*exp(-beta*2)*exp(gamma*(t[i] - 2))
  - If t>h then: A = (A0*exp(bi))*exp(-beta*2)*exp(gamma*(h-2)) *exp(-alpha(t[i] - h))
Here h is also a parameter to be estimated.

So I have the Stan code as following:
child   <- read.csv('data_childcens_4Cov27Jun16.csv', sep = ",", dec='.', header=T, na.strings = '.'); head(child)
child$ID<- paste("A", child$id, sep = ""); child$ID <- as.factor(child$ID); str(child)
N       <- nrow(child); N                                                      #302
cens    <- subset(child, CENS ==1 & t > 4); str(cens)

#-------------------- Data for Stan
stan_dat<- list(subj = as.integer(child$ID),
           N    = N,
           J    = nlevels(child$ID),
           y    = child$y_new,
           time = child$t,
           cens = child$CENS)

#------------------- Stan code for running model with random A0 only, no covariate.
model_string <- "
data {
     int<lower=1> N;                         // Total number of data points
     real<lower=0> time[N];                  // Time points
     real<lower=0, upper = 3> y[N];          // Antibody levels on log10 scale
     int<lower=1>     J;                     // Number of subjects
     int<lower=1, upper=J>    subj[N];       // Subject id
     int<lower=0, upper=1>    cens[N];       // Child1 or Child2
}

parameters {
     real<lower=0> beta;
     real<lower=0> gamma;
     real<lower=4> h;
     real<lower=0> alpha;
     vector[J] b;                          //subj intercept
     real<lower=0> A0;
     real<lower=0> sigma_A0;
     real<lower=0> sigma;

}

model {
     real mu;
     // Priors
     b ~ normal(0, sigma_A0);           //subj random effects
     // Likelihood
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( (time[i] <= 2) && (cens[i] ==0) ) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-beta*time[i])) ;
            increment_log_prob(normal_log(y, mu, sigma)); }
        else if ( (2< time[i] <= h) && (cens[i] ==0) ) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-2*beta) * exp(gamma*(time[i]-2)) ) ;
            increment_log_prob(normal_log(y, mu, sigma)); }
        else if ( (time[i] > h) && (cens[i] ==0) ) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-2*beta) * exp(gamma*(h-2)) * exp(-alpha*(time[i]-h)) );
            increment_log_prob(normal_log(y, mu, sigma)); }
        else if ((time[i] <= 2) && (cens[i] ==1)) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-beta*time[i])) ;
            increment_log_prob(normal_cdf_log(y,mu,sigma));}
        else if ( (2< time[i] <= h) && (cens[i] ==1) ) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-2*beta) * exp(gamma*(time[i]-2)) ) ;
            increment_log_prob(normal_cdf_log(y,mu,sigma));}
        else if ((time[i] > h) && (cens[i] ==1)) {
            mu = log10( (A0*exp(b[subj[i]])) * exp(-2*beta) * exp(gamma*(h-2)) * exp(-alpha*(time[i]-h)) );
            increment_log_prob(normal_cdf_log(y,mu,sigma));}
}
}
"

mcmc.sample <- stan(model_code=model_string, data=stan_dat, pars=c('A0','beta','gamma','alpha','h',
                                                                   'sigma','sigma_A0'),
                    chains=1, iter=10000, warmup=5000)
                    #control=list(adapt_delta=0.99, stepsize = 0.01, max_treedepth =15))

print(mcmc.sample, pars=c('A0','beta','gamma','alpha','h','sigma','sigma_A0'), probs=c(0.25,0.50,0.7

Since I test the model on the simulated data, but the output really shocks me: Parameter estimates for alpha and h are extremely large.
Here are the outputs (on another simulated data set): 
                  mean se_mean   sd           25%           50%           75% n_eff Rhat
A0        1.006000e+01    0.13 0.34  9.780000e+00  1.006000e+01  1.033000e+01     7 1.05
beta      1.000000e-02    0.00 0.00  0.000000e+00  1.000000e-02  1.000000e-02     4 1.69
gamma     1.000000e-02    0.00 0.00  1.000000e-02  1.000000e-02  1.000000e-02    73 1.03
alpha    8.238175e+307     Inf  Inf 3.534001e+307 7.759250e+307 1.284784e+308  5000  NaN
h        9.233497e+307     Inf  Inf 5.087358e+307 9.159453e+307 1.360775e+308  5000  NaN
sigma     4.400000e-01    0.00 0.00  4.400000e-01  4.400000e-01  4.400000e-01   401 1.00
sigma_A0  6.500000e-01    0.00 0.05  6.100000e-01  6.400000e-01  6.700000e-01   149 1.04


I spent 2 days to figure out what is going on but I can not see where the fault is.
If anybody has an idea here?

I attach the simuated data for your run.
Thanks.

parts:
I'd highly recommend standard formatting (I sound like a broken record
here on our lists about this because it's hard for me and others
to read programs written this way---you should be writing programs so
they can be read, just like any other writing).

I don't think there's any truncation case where you just want
to increment with the CDF. But if you have censored values,
you do want to use the CDFs, but then you don't want to use
the densities. Not sure if that'll help, but then I
don't understand this model.

For numerical stability and efficiency, all those exp() are bad news.
I'd at least use exp(a) * exp(b) = exp(a + b) to simplify. Even better
if you can just keep everything on the log scale.

Also, is there a reason there's no intercept in those regressions?
That'd be either a mean parameter for b in the centered parameterization
or an addition of a mean-like parameter in the non-centered parameterization.

- Bob

Hi Bob,
Thank you for your reply.

I find hard to write the program as a standard formatting as I have a non-linear mixed model where the antibody levels depend on time, and also I have left-censored values.
Basically, I want to write a Stan program which are identical to the following program that I already wrote in SAS (and hope with this SAS code, it is clearer what I am trying to write):

proc nlmixed data = childnew xtol = 1E-12 method = GAUSS qpoints = 100;
   parms A0 =9.54 beta = 0.542 gamma = 0.518 alpha = 0.317 h = 7.22
         sigma2_A0 = 1.09
         sigma2 = 0.1;
   bounds A0 beta gamma alpha > 0;
   bounds sigma2_A0 sigma2>= 0;
   pi = constant('pi');
   mu1 = (A0*exp(A0_i))*exp(-beta*t);
   mu2 = (A0*exp(A0_i))*exp(-beta*2)*exp((t-2)*gamma);
   mu3 = (A0*exp(A0_i))*exp(-beta*2)*exp((h-2)*gamma)*exp(-alpha*(t-h));
   if t<= 2 and cens=0 then
     ll = (1/(sqrt(2*pi*sigma2)))*exp(-(ynew - log10(mu1))**2/ (2*sigma2));
   if t>2 and t <= h and cens=0 then
     ll = (1/(sqrt(2*pi*sigma2)))*exp(-(ynew - log10(mu2))**2/ (2*sigma2));
   if t > h and cens=0 then
     ll = (1/(sqrt(2*pi*sigma2)))*exp(-(ynew - log10(mu3))**2/ (2*sigma2));
   if t<= 2 and cens=1 then
     ll = probnorm((ynew - log10(mu1)) / sqrt(sigma2));
   if t>2 and t <= h and cens=1 then
     ll = probnorm((ynew - log10(mu2)) / sqrt(sigma2));
   if t > h and cens=1 then
     ll = probnorm((ynew - log10(mu3)) / sqrt(sigma2));
   L = log(ll); /*Log-likelihood*/
   model ynew ~ general(L);
   random A0_i ~ normal(0,sigma2_A0)
          subject = ID;
  run; quit;


So based on different scenario, either I would like to use the density or a cumulative distribution function.
Also, as I mentioned earlier, I assumed the antibody level at birth (A0,i) of each individual has a log-normal distribution, so: A0,i = A0*exp(bi) where bi ~ lognormal distribution. That is the intension of the model.

Thank you if you can give me any hint.

parts:
Uhm,
I think now I know where the problem comes from.
Instead of using: (2< time[i] <= h), I should use time[i] >2 && time[i] <h instead. Now the parameter estimates are reasonable for me.

Thao.
